title: TeleProt-guided engineering yields a nuclease variant with improved neutral-pH biofilm degradation
summary: A machine-learning-guided design and high-throughput screening campaign produced a Bacillus licheniformis NucB variant with 19-fold higher measured specific activity than wild type at pH 7. At 1 μM in a laboratory biofilm assay at neutral pH, the selected variant degraded 71% ± 2% of the biofilm versus 13% ± 3% for wild-type NucB.
ai_technology: TeleProt machine-learning-guided protein-library design framework; best-performing ML3 variant selected by model-based optimization with a deep neural network (MBO-DNN)
organization: X, the Moonshot Factory; Google DeepMind; Triplebar; University of Cambridge

evidence.tested: A machine-learning-guided design and high-throughput screening campaign produced a Bacillus licheniformis NucB variant with 19-fold higher measured specific activity than wild type at pH 7.
evidence.unknown: The evidence is from enzyme and in-vitro B. licheniformis biofilm assays; it does not show wound healing, animal efficacy or clinical benefit. At the 1 μM dose, the paper reports the stated biofilm comparison; conditions and estimates are study-specific. This is engineering of a known nuclease, not discovery of a naturally new enzyme or organismal mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: TeleProt combined sequence-evolutionary information with experimental genotype–phenotype data to propose diverse NucB variants for high-throughput microfluidic activity screening. The selected ML-guided variant was then purified and assessed in a lower-throughput nuclease assay and a neutral-pH biofilm degradation assay.
